symptom: `.claude/bootstrap-mxcli.sh` on Windows (Git Bash) with no mxcli on PATH: `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404` for `.../nightly/mxcli-mingw64_nt-10.0-26200-amd64`, and the session starts without mxcli because the hook runs `sh .claude/bootstrap-mxcli.sh || true`
cause: The download asset name was `mxcli-$(uname -s | tr A-Z a-z)-<arch>`. Under Git Bash, MSYS2 and Cygwin `uname -s` is `MINGW64_NT-10.0-26200` / `MSYS_NT-…` / `CYGWIN_NT-…`, never `windows`, and the Windows release assets carry `.exe`. The script also hard-coded `./mxcli` as its binary path everywhere
insight: **`uname -s` is a kernel name, not a GOOS.** Mapping it to the release asset needs the same table the Makefile `release` target uses for its output names (linux/darwin/windows plus `.exe`), and that table is easy to check against. The script's tests only ran on Linux, so no test ever hit the Windows branch, and `requireSh` skips Windows CI anyway. A fake `uname` on PATH reaches every platform branch from a Linux runner, and the curl stand-in must log the URL: before this fix it logged only the output file, which is why a wrong asset name could not fail any test. Detect the platform once at the top and keep the binary path in one variable (`$MXCLI` = `./mxcli` or `./mxcli.exe`); otherwise every `[ -x ./mxcli ]` guard has to rely on MSYS's implicit `.exe` lookup. On Windows, remove a stray non-executable `./mxcli` (the Linux build `mxcli new` leaves) before installing `./mxcli.exe`, because Git Bash resolves the exact name first. Remove it before the install and not after, since Cygwin's `rm ./mxcli` can also take `mxcli.exe`
